title: Longest Word Chain
statement:
Given an array of lowercase English `words`, a word `a` is a **predecessor** of word `b` if and only if inserting exactly one letter anywhere in `a` (without reordering the remaining letters) produces `b`. For example, `"cat"` is a predecessor of `"chat"`, while `"tac"` is not.

A **word chain** is a sequence `[w_1, w_2, ..., w_k]` (`k >= 1`) where each `w_i` is a predecessor of `w_{i+1}` and every word comes from `words`. Return the maximum possible length of a word chain.

Contract
- `words` may be empty (return `0`) and may contain duplicates (duplicates do not extend a chain because a predecessor must be strictly 1 character shorter).
- Word lengths are positive and words are not guaranteed to be sorted.

Examples
- `["a", "at", "cat", "chat", "chart", "dog"]` -> `5` (`"a" -> "at" -> "cat" -> "chat" -> "chart"`).
- `["in", "pin", "spin", "spine", "spline", "on"]` -> `5` (`"in" -> "pin" -> "spin" -> "spine" -> "spline"`).
- `["team", "jira"]` -> `1` (no word is a predecessor of another).

hints: Because every step increases word length by 1, sorting the words by ascending length guarantees that all possible predecessors of word w are processed before w.

Let dp[w] be the length of the longest word chain ending at w (initialized to 1). For each word w of length L, generate each of its L candidate predecessors by deleting one character at index i (0 <= i < L).

Look up each candidate predecessor in a HashMap<String, Integer> dp; set dp[w] = max(dp[w], dp.getOrDefault(pred, 0) + 1) and track the global maximum. Intended complexity: O(n log n + n * L^2) time (O(n log n) for bounded L), O(n * L) space.
